findings.title: Hörprofil erklärt echten gewichteten Skip nach Podcast fälschlich als folgenlosen Opener
findings.preconditions: One legitimate extended-history file in chronological order. Music play followed by an approximately58min podcast followed immediately by music skipped after3s. All entries before liveSince. reason_start=trackdone (no restart).
steps: Import music play ended2026-09-25T01:59:54Z(ms180000), podcast ended02:59:54Z(ms3500000, spotify_track_uri:null), skipped song ended02:59:57Z(ms3000, reason_start:trackdone, reason_end:fwdbtn)
Run aggregateHistory and importHistory(toRows(aggregate),0,1), then addListens/finishListens and actual two-block importListens
findings.expected: One consistent classification. Under explicit podcast-keeps-listening rule this is ordinary early skip; profile early1/openers0 and actual memory weight0.5. UI must not claim skippedId is exempt from downweighting.
findings.cause: aggregateHistory tracks any finite-timestamp entry including podcast. addListens drops podcasts. Hub.timeline recomputes silence using music-only rows and infers opener from the artificial hour gap.
findings.impact: Owner-facing profile reports a false exemption from taste suppression; same imported event drives ordinary skip reduction in planner while UI promises no reduction. This is correctness/honest-state regression introduced by new opener classification.
findings.repair_direction: Preserve shared opener classification/activity continuity before dropping nonmusic entries; do not infer genuine silence from lossy music-only rows. Keep old-row compatibility and file-boundary policy explicit.
required_regressions: old imported rows and multiple files remain compatible

non_findings.detail: First skip in eachfile intentionally assumes unknown prior activity, so aggregated opener can differ from globally joined music profile. Reproduced discrepancy; not claimed separately as defect because PR explicitly states this policy.
